purpose: Reusable writing instructions abstracted from user-supplied completed reports. No patient-specific text is included. Not a verified legal standard or model fine-tuning.
general: Match the template headings and write clear professional clinical prose. Use several focused sentences when evidence warrants detail; do not pad short evidence to imitate sample length.
Connect documented symptoms and findings to documented functional effects. Attribute interpretations and preserve limitations and contradictions.
Use chronological and comparative reasoning across records without merging patient identities or treating historical findings as current.
Example reports teach style and organization only. Never transfer example facts, measurements, diagnoses, codes, signatures, prognosis, legal opinions, fees or clinical plans into the current case.

jane_evaluation: Use the clinic section order. Begin with the patient presentation and dated collision/intake chronology; describe onset, location, intensity, provoking/relieving factors and associated symptoms where documented.
Expand body-chart, vitals, posture, ROM and neurological sections only from actual documented answers or clinician measurements. Attribute intake diagrams as subjective.
Use practical function and patient goals to explain the complaint. Keep clinician assessment, planned care and home instructions distinct from patient expectations.
jane_soap: Write encounter-specific paragraphs: interval symptoms and functional tolerance, documented objective changes, treatment actually delivered, response and clinician plan.
Compare baseline and current pain, ROM or function only when both dated measurements are documented. Distinguish new findings from carried-forward history.
Describe treatment region, technique, modality, units/time and response only if documented; give CPT rationale only from supplied clinician rationale and services.
soap: Subjective: symptoms, onset/history, modifiers, medication response and functional limitations, attributed to patient.
Objective: dated measured examination and reported diagnostic findings; no normal defaults.
Assessment and plan: documented clinician diagnosis, interpretation, course, response and decisions. Preserve partial useful sections when other sections are unsupported.
physician: Use a coherent chronological history before diagnoses, objective findings, outcome measures, professional opinion, work effects, prognosis and planned care.
Organize clinician-documented diagnoses by involved region and include supplied codes without choosing new diagnoses from symptoms.
Retain measured scores, scale name, date and documented interpretation; do not reuse example thresholds or calculate impairment from an outcome score.
Attribute clinician causation and medical-necessity opinions. Distinguish an initial projected care course from actual subsequent discharge.
dud_loe: For each template activity category, describe the specific task, prior baseline, reported symptom during the task, tolerance/modification, timing and real-life effect when supplied.
Use concrete occupational, domestic, household, childcare, sport and hobby descriptions; avoid repeating generic pain claims across all sections.
Distinguish missed work from working with discomfort; reduced tolerance does not establish lost wages, job insecurity, disability or stopped hobbies.
Preserve activities that remain possible and documented absences of limitations. Do not import the example occupation, family situation or tasks.
narrative: Present the treatment span and verified administrative totals, collision/history, pre-existing conditions, region-specific findings, diagnostic testing, care course, response, discharge status and future clinician recommendations in template order.
Build a dated baseline-to-final comparison with actual findings and functional changes; distinguish projected from delivered treatment.
Describe residual symptoms separately from clinician-established permanent impairment, disability or MMI. Do not assign ratings or infer MMI from improvement alone.
Future-care frequency, duration, fees and prognosis must come from this case's clinician and financial sources; sample schedules and costs are never defaults.
imaging: Summarize supplied radiologist/clinician findings by region and reported level; preserve measurements, negatives, limitations and author attribution.
Separate imaging observations, existing clinician interpretation, and documented recommendations. No independent diagnosis from raw images or dating a lesion without supporting opinion.
mri: Use the sample structure: indication, study/date and source, reported findings by region/level, conclusion, existing clinician correlation, verified literature if supplied, and documented recommendations.
Preserve reported disc, canal, foraminal, cord and other findings without treating degenerative findings as automatically accident-caused.
Do not interpret MRI screenshots independently; summaries must be based on a supplied radiology report or explicit clinician interpretation.
Only include literature whose source and relevance have been verified; never fabricate studies, author names or guideline endorsements.
cover: Write a concise professional transmittal: purpose, relevant accident/treatment dates if documented, exact enclosure list, contact closing.
List only documents actually supplied or confirmed prepared; do not claim a complete packet, executed lien or signed report exists without evidence.
Do not reproduce sample recipient, contact information, provider identifiers or signatures.
billing: Reproduce documented statement identity/period, itemized service entries, supplied amounts and account summary with citations.
Keep charge, payment, adjustment, insurer/attorney and patient ledger allocations distinct; a duplicate allocation is not a second delivered service.
Do not infer CPT codes, timed units or payable charges from narrative treatment descriptions. Do not calculate or assert ledger reconciliation with the language model.
Copy documented totals as reported and flag conflicting counts/amounts for financial review. This draft is a source summary, not an issued invoice.
lien: Retain the clinic-provided fixed bilingual legal wording; populate only verified case/administrative details.
Never reuse a sample patient authorization, attorney, signature, witness, execution date or attestation.
The model must not rewrite the approved legal body or assert legal validity from sample wording.
packet: The complete medical file is a packet containing individual documents, not one new clinical note. Keep document boundaries and dates.
Avoid double-counting care or charges when the same chart/report occurs as a separate upload and inside a complete packet.
A packet manifest must list actual prepared files; formatting style does not establish completeness or authorization to send.
